subject: Temporary version hold request for Atlas-v2 variants — SLO vs roadmap tradeoffs
messages:
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: serving-team@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com, lauren_bishop@redwood.com
Cc: eng-ops@orbit-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Temporary version hold request for Atlas-v2 variants — SLO vs roadmap tradeoffs

Team — quick context and ask.

We started the Atlas-v2 rollout to production-sized clusters yesterday night. Staging telemetry is showing a consistent P95 latency increase for the v2-XL variants on our low-latency customer routes (notably Orbit Analytics, schema-based responses) — roughly a 15–40ms regression versus v1 at similar QPS and sequence lengths. The product team is concerned because this directly impacts those customers' SLOs.

Ask: approve a temporary hold on automatic rollouts of Atlas-v2-XL to low-latency routes for 24–48 hours while we triage and implement mitigations. This is not a global block; we want to keep model availability for non-latency-sensitive traffic.

What I looked at so far:
- Dashboard: https://redwood.console/dash/atlas-v2-regression (screenshots attached)
- Early hypothesis: quantization heuristics + kernel selection differences for XL sequences interacting poorly with our short-window attention optimizations.

Suggested mitigation steps (we can iterate):
1) Soft hold policy: block auto-rollout for routes tagged with "low-latency" and route those to Atlas-v2-slim or v1 for 24–48h.
2) Run a controlled canary (20% traffic to XL, 80% to slim) with stricter latency SLO gating.
3) Enable prefix KV caching for impacted routes and bump autoscaler thresholds temporarily.

Attachments: latency_regression_screenshots.png, proposal_hold_and-mitigation.md.

Open questions I need answered before I approve broadly:
- Can infra implement the hold + targeted routing quickly?
- Do we have an easy way to pin Dedicated customers (Orbit) to v1 or slim variant without manual config churn?
- Is there a quick kernel/quantization rollback plan if needed?

I want to be conservative here — if we can't get a reliable canary within the next 12 hours, I'm inclined to hold rollouts to those routes. Appreciate quick responses.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Product Manager, Model Onboarding
Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, serving-team@redwood.com
Cc: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, eng-ops@orbit-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary version hold request for Atlas-v2 variants — SLO vs roadmap tradeoffs

On Sat, Nov 21, 2026 at 09:12 AM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — quick context and ask.
> ...

Thanks for the heads-up, Kim. A few technical clarifications so we can scope the work and time-to-hold: 

1) Telemetry: can you attach the exact staging run ids / trace ids? I want to check kernel selection logs & perf counters. If you can paste two trace ids we can correlate to the perf dashboard.
2) Quantization / kernels: if the XL variant is falling back to a slower kernel path at certain seq lengths, we may be able to force a quantization-profile downgrade for the canary only (fast path) while we instrument. I need to know which quant config was used for the rollout (q8_0 / q4x4 etc.).
3) Routing: routing a Dedicated customer to v1/slim should be doable through a per-customer variant override; I’ll need the Orbit customer id. For hosted routes, we can create a route tag and short-circuit the admission policy.

Operational ask: if we put a 24h hold, I want to run a narrow canary first (10–20% traffic) to validate kernel/quant changes before widening. If that canary passes latency gates for 6 hours, we can re-evaluate. If it does not, we roll back XL entirely for those routes.

I can prototype the quant-profile toggle in the next 3–4 hours if someone shares the rollout artifact id.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>, eng-ops@orbit-analytics.com
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 13:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary version hold request for Atlas-v2 variants — SLO vs roadmap tradeoffs

Thanks — I ran a quick risk/impact assessment with CS and infra. Proposed operational plan below (low churn, limits customer impact):

Immediate (within 2h):
- Apply targeted hold: create an "atlas-v2-hold-20261121" rollout policy that blocks auto-promote for any route with tag "low-latency". (Effect: hosted customers tagged low-latency route to slim or v1).
- For Orbit Analytics (Dedicated): apply per-customer override to pin to atlas-v1 for the next 48h.
- Kick off a 20% canary to XL on a separate cluster with quant-profile forced to q8_0 (fast path). Canary gating: 6h windows, fail on p95 > baseline + 10ms.

Short term (24–48h):
- Enable prefix KV caching for affected pathways. That should shave 8–12ms on p95 for repeated prompts.
- Temporarily increase autoscaler headroom for canary cluster + bump pre-warm slots.
- Attach: canary-playbook.pdf with step-by-step.

Rollback plan:
- If canary fails two consecutive 6h windows, we roll XL back off production for low-latency routes and open an incident. Triage will focus on kernel selection and quantization config.

Impact: expected ~5% increase in cost for 48h due to autoscaler bump; CS notified Orbit and created a short customer note.

If everyone agrees, I'll enact the rollout policy and start the canary.

--
Lauren Bishop
Director, Platform Product
Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: lauren_bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, vivek_kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Cc: eng-ops@orbit-analytics.com
Date: Sun, 22 Nov 2026 16:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Temporary version hold request for Atlas-v2 variants — SLO vs roadmap tradeoffs

I've created INF-9421 to track the hold + canary work (https://jira.redwood.com/browse/INF-9421). Action items I completed / will do in the next 6 hours:
- Created rollout policy atlas-v2-hold-20261121 and applied to tagged routes.
- Applied per-customer override for Orbit Analytics (customer id orbit-998) to atlas-v1.
- Standing up canary cluster with forced q8_0 quant-profile; starting 20% split now.
- Enabled KV prefix cache for the canary group.

Monitoring: I wired the canary to a dedicated dashboard and set alerts for p50/p95/p99 regressions. If we hit p95 > baseline + 10ms for two consecutive windows, I'll flip rollback and stop the canary.

Cost note: estimated +4–6% infra delta while canary runs; I will put a flag in the ticket if we exceed that.

Approving the temporary hold as requested. Will keep this thread updated and ping on the incident channel if automatic rollback triggers.

Dev Patel
Staff Software Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
